correctness.rationale: One-step two-node trapezoidal exponentiation reduces exactly to u_{k+1}=c e^{-u_k} and predictor u0>W0(c). Its continuous increasing second iterate has monotone bounded even subsequences; the strictly monotone c(d) cycle parametrization proves the unique-cycle/no-cycle dichotomy. The repelling derivative W0(c)^2>1 excludes convergence to the fixed point above e. A third-order expansion of T^2 at c=e proves the signed sqrt(k) law. The threshold equations and the strict carrying-capacity-safe interval follow from Lambert W and the strict logarithm inequality. The standalone program independently checks 13321 deterministic finite assertions; these tests are corroborative rather than infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A concrete method-selection gap: unconditional positive finite corrections do not guarantee that adding sweeps converges to the collocation solution. The exact fixed-a threshold, uniform h=2 frontier, attracting two-cycle and open window of sweep failure with a valid collocation endpoint quantify this failure and the high-correction regime in the smallest natural nontrivial Gauss–Lobatto case. The critical sweep-rate quantifies computational slowdowns even at the boundary. This is a complete parameter classification, not an arbitrary numerical instance or a routine finite table.
